title: nutty dutch mussels bouillabaisse
description: a floral and creamy dutch dish featuring massaman-paste, mortar-pestled pesto, and mediterranean-friendly flavors.
instructions: heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.

add the mussels, massaman paste, garlic, onion, lemon, whiskey, mussel bouillon, crème fraîche, heavy cream, fresh parsley, fresh dill, salt, black pepper, nutmeg, and cayenne pepper to the saucepan and stir to combine.
bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 5 minutes.
mash the mussels with a potato masher or the back of a spoon until they are well broken down.
stir in the mortar-pestled pesto, butter, sun-dried tomatoes, chopped fresh chives, grated ginger, fennel seeds, ground cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper.
season with salt and black pepper to taste.
serve the mussels hot, garnished with fresh parsley and fresh dill.
melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
add the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture forms a smooth paste.
slowly add the white wine and fish stock, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened slightly.
stir in the capers, chopped scallions, and grated ginger.
season with salt, black pepper, and nutmeg to taste.
serve the sauce hot over the mussels.
